Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; David Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects: first, our organic sales growth rate; second, our promotional strategy and its effectiveness; third, the performance of our marketing campaigns; and fourth, a summary of our financial results and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to David Reynolds to provide more detail on our financial results.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.4 billion, representing a 6% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis. Gross margin expanded to 46.1%, driven by productivity gains from our Project Horizon initiative, favorable commodity hedging, and supply chain optimizations. Operating income was $3.2 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.22 adjusted, up 11% year over year. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me expand on these results with more granularity, starting with our organic sales growth rate. We achieved 4.2% organic sales growth for the quarter, exceeding our guided range of 2% to 3% and representing the third straight quarter of accelerating momentum. Year-to-date through nine months, organic growth stands at 3.8%, positioning us well to hit our full-year target of 3% to 4%. This result highlights the durability of our core consumer packaged goods portfolio against ongoing macroeconomic pressures, such as moderating but still elevated inflation in key inputs like cocoa, palm oil, and edible oils.

For clarity, organic growth strips out acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange effects. On an FX-neutral basis, the 4.2% reflects an even split of 2.1% volume growth and 2.1% price/mix improvement. This balanced dynamic is crucial in our industry following the pricing actions of 2022 and 2023, as consumer elasticity normalizes. Volumes turned positive last quarter and are gaining traction, with consumers returning to branded staples—supported by IRI and Nielsen scanner data showing us capturing 110 basis points of market share in North American grocery channels.

Diving into segments for sharper insight: Our Health & Wellness division, which accounts for 42% of sales, posted 6.8% organic growth. Innovation led the way, with the NutriBoost protein snack line—now featuring 15% plant-based options—delivering double-digit sales velocity in club stores like Costco and Sam's Club. Premiumization boosted price/mix by 4%, favoring high-margin formats such as single-serve pouches, aligning with industry shifts toward functional nutrition amid GLP-1 medication trends, much like strategies from Kellogg's and General Mills.

Beverages advanced 3.5% organically, with 1.8% volume gains from PureSpring zero-sugar sparkling waters, which gained distribution in 5,000 more U.S. convenience stores through our Casey's General Stores partnership. Price/mix added 1.7%, leveraging elastic pricing in emerging hydration categories, where SPINS data shows us outperforming private labels by 300 basis points.

Beauty & Personal Care grew 2.9%, with volumes up 0.9% amid category softness. FreshGlow's clean beauty offerings thrived via e-commerce, now 22% of division sales versus 15% last year, driven by direct-to-consumer subscriptions and Amazon optimizations. Our sustainability edge—100% recyclable packaging on core SKUs—helps us compete against Unilever's Dove and P&G's Olay.

Geographically, gains were widespread: North America, 65% of sales, hit 5.1% organic growth, with 1.2 points of distribution expansion in perimeter-of-store placements per 84.51 analytics, countering center-store weakness and gaining against Aldi and Lidl in dollar channels. EMEA, 18% of sales, managed 2.4%, hampered by deflation in Germany and the UK but boosted by 7% volumes in France and Iberia from tailored household promotions. APAC, 10%, reached 4.7%, with China volumes up 3% post-COVID via Tmall and JD.com, and India hypermarkets adding 500 basis points to distribution. Latin America, 7%, saw 1.8%, limited by Argentina's hyperinflation but lifted by 5% Brazil volumes on value nutrition packs.

This success builds on three foundational strategies from our 2023 portfolio realignment: a robust innovation pipeline, where 22% of Q3 sales came from products launched within the past two years—like low/no-alcohol ready-to-drinks and microbiome skincare; enhanced supply chain resilience through nearshoring, with our U.S. Midwest facility now sourcing 40% domestically to slash lead times by 25% and cap input inflation at 3% versus the industry's 8%; and route-to-market enhancements, including an 18% SKU reduction to 1,200 focus items, while penetrating dollar stores (15% of North America sales) and quick-commerce via DoorDash and Instacart.

Moving forward, easing inflation—CPI ex-food at 2.5%—should aid volume rebound, though we watch private label pushes and APAC tariffs closely. We guide Q4 organic growth to 3.5% to 4.5%, with full-year EPS growth of 7% to 8% at midpoint.

Shifting to our promotional strategy and effectiveness, which fueled much of this quarter's volume. Total trade spend was 18.7% of net sales, down 120 basis points year over year to 19.9%, in line with our full-year goal of 18% to 19% and better than peers like Procter & Gamble's 20-22%. We're reallocating to efficient, data-informed tactics rather than slashing volume drivers. Promo ROI— incremental gross profit per dollar spent—reached 3.8x, up from 3.2x last year, our best in three years, with 15% sales lift from base and incremental volume, and just 8% cannibalization per IRI and Nielsen panels.

In Snacks & Beverages, 45% of revenue, we focused on event-driven promotions for back-to-school and NFL season. CrunchTime pretzels and ZipFizz energy drinks featured 12-week programs at Walmart and Kroger, securing 22% ACV distribution and 14% volume uplift above the 9% category norm. EDLP on multipacks at $3.99 grew household penetration 28%, while 20-25% TPRs on singles yielded 3.5x ROI. Our AI dynamic pricing, linked to Kroger's Precision Marketing, cut poor performers by 25% and spiked Gen Z penetration 18%, with their digital coupon redemptions 2.2x higher than boomers.

For Household & Personal Care, 35% of sales, we emphasized loyalty amid private label threats. Sustainability-tied promos for EcoClean laundry pods and PureGlow skincare partnered with Target Circle for buy-5-get-1-free, hitting 3.2x ROI and 11% share gains. VMI with machine learning optimized terms, lifting our promo score (lift, ROI, margin blend) to 87/100 from 76, preserving 42.1% gross margins despite 7% surfactant inflation.

Regionally, North America (75% sales) drove 5.1% organic via omnichannel, like 19% lifts at Walmart+ for ThirstQuench bundles. Canada trailed at 2.8% but Quebec digital ads boosted 12%. Europe (15%) navigated HFSS rules with health-focused deals, like 15% off low-sugar CrunchTime at Carrefour for 4.3x ROI and 7% share versus Mondelez; Germany hit 9% via Edeka. APAC/LATAM (10%) excelled in China Double 11 for ZipFizz at 6.5x ROI and Brazil TPRs at 2.8x against Ambev.

Tech upgrades like PromoOptix AI on Snowflake simulate thousands of scenarios at 92% accuracy, slashing underperformers 30%; GS1/blockchain cuts fraud 40%; Instacart/DoorDash pilots boost repeats 15%. We balance volume-margin with -2.4 elasticity in snacks, reclaiming 200 bps gross margin by axing low-ROI and shifting 25% of $450M budget to digital (2.7x ROAS per Kantar). Q4 targets 4.0x+ ROI with AI chatbots.

Now, on marketing campaign effectiveness, our investments drove outsized results amid 4-5% staple inflation and 1.2-point private label share erosion. Blended ROAS hit 4.8x, up from 3.9x last year—our strongest in three years—versus flat category sales per IRI/Nielsen. A&P spend was $1.2 billion, steady at 12.5% of sales, but reallocated 25% to high-ROI like retail media and CTV.

Measurement advanced with MTA via The Trade Desk and first-party data, using geo-holdouts for 22% penetration lift on CrispWave snacks. A 45-day window captures 28% repeat rates for exposed households versus 19%.

Channels evolved: Retail media at 28% mix (from 15%) yielded 7.2x ROAS; Amazon/Walmart Connect powered AquaPure's Refresh Revolution to 10.8x on $4.2M for $45M sales. TikTok/Instagram UGC for GlowEssence AR filters gave 3.5x engagement ROAS, lifting Gen Z skincare to 22% volume. CTV on Hulu/Roku for BigBite patties hit 5.1x with 78% completion; linear TV cut to 22%. Micro-influencers at 6.2x outperformed.

North America (55% sales) led at 5.3x ROAS; Fuel Your Hustle for energy bars gained 1.4 points share to 14.2%, e-comm up 32% AOV $28.50. EMEA at 6.0x countered regs with PurePlanet on Pinterest/Tesco for 9% eco-volume. APAC 4.2x, China KOLs 12.5x for BeautyBloom, India JioMart 17% trial. LATAM 3.8x stabilized Fiesta chips.

AI MarkOptix predicts 88% accurately, speeding tests; CLV focus grew loyalty to 42M members at $245 annual. Q4 guides 4.5-5.0x ROAS on $1.3B A&P for 5-7% organic.

Wrapping with a full summary of financial results and outlook. Q3 net sales $15.4 billion, up 6% reported and 4.2% organic—11th consecutive positive quarter, beating category 4% per NielsenIQ. Volumes/mix +3 points from share in snacks/beverages; pricing +5 points, including 2% in Beauty & Personal Care for packaging/palm costs.

Adjusted gross profit $7.1 billion, up 10%, margin +220 bps to 46.1% via $500M Project Horizon (plant consolidations, 85% hedging), moderating cocoa (-15%). SG&A 25.4% (-80 bps) from zero-based budgeting, AI revenue tools saving $150M like P&G's. Operating income $3.2B (+12%), margin 20.8% (+140 bps). Adjusted EPS $1.22 (+11%, beat $0.05).

Segments: Nutrition & Hydration (45%) 10% organic on low-sugar drinks; Snacks 7% with nuts +2 points share; Beauty 4%. Regions: NA 9%, EMEA 6% (FX -200 bps, laundry gains vs Unilever), APAC 11% (India oral care), LATAM 7%.

FCF $2.1B (14% sales), $1.2B buybacks, dividend $0.48 (+27th year). Leverage 2.1x, $8B liquidity.

FY2024 outlook raised: organic 6.5-7.5% (from 6-7%), EPS +9-11% ($4.85-4.95) with $100M extra savings, margins 45.5-46%, op 20.5%, $200M FX drag. Q4 organic 7-8%, EPS $1.28-1.32. Tailwinds: 3% CPI, e-comm 18%, imperatives like health premiumization (15 SKUs), 40% recyclable packaging, $300M precision commerce.

Risks: tariffs, weather, private label. But our portfolio and innovation set us up to win.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Doe with JPMorgan.

John Doe:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks for the question, John. Inflation has undeniably shaped consumer behavior, but our brands have shown remarkable resilience. As David outlined, we've seen volumes inflect positively, with 2.1% growth in Q3 organic sales amid sticky commodity costs like cocoa and oils. Consumers are trading back to branded staples, gaining us 110 bps share in North America per IRI/Nielsen. In Health & Wellness, NutriBoost's plant-based innovations captured double-digit velocity in clubs, while PureSpring's hydration functionals outpaced private labels by 300 bps. Regionally, North America's 5.1% growth reflects value-pack shifts as CPI eases to 2.5% ex-food. EMEA's 2.4% held despite deflation, buoyed by localized promotions. Our pricing discipline—2.1% mix/price—offsets elasticity resets post-2022 hikes, and promo ROI at 3.8x ensures we're not just chasing volume but protecting margins at 46.1%. Marketing ROAS of 4.8x reinforces this, with retail media driving targeted reach. We're monitoring private label aggression and GLP-1 effects, but nearshoring limits our input inflation to 3%, positioning us for sustained recovery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Chen:
Thanks. Regarding your new product, NutriBoost protein snacks, what are the projections for its market impact?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. NutriBoost, with its expanded 15% plant-based SKUs, has been a standout in Health & Wellness, contributing to the segment's 6.8% organic growth. In Q3, it posted double-digit velocity gains in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club, mirroring functional nutrition trends boosted by GLP-1 adoption. Premium single-serve pouches drove 4% price/mix, aligning with peers like Kellogg's. Projections for full-year: we expect it to represent 5% of division sales, with market share gains of 150 bps in protein snacks per IRI. Q4 tailwinds include back-to-school extensions and holiday bundles via Walmart Connect, targeting 20% volume growth. Marketing-wise, our Fuel Your Hustle campaign integrates CTV and Instacart for 5.5x projected ROAS, lifting household penetration 25%. E-comm DTC subscriptions now fuel repeat rates at 35%, with Gen Z uptake at 28% of volume. Long-term, in the $50B functional market, we'll launch three variants next year, aiming for $300M incremental revenue by FY2026, supported by sustainability claims and AR try-ons on TikTok.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Barclays.

Mike Rossi:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

David Reynolds:
Sure, Mike. Promotional spending was tightly managed at 18.7% of sales, down 120 bps YoY, with ROI surging to 3.8x—our best in years. This funded 60% of volume growth without margin erosion. In Snacks & Beverages, event promos like NFL/back-to-school at Walmart/Kroger hit 14% uplift, 3.5x ROI on TPRs, aided by AI pricing cutting waste 25%. Household shifted to loyalty like Target Circle for 3.2x ROI, 87/100 effectiveness score. PromoOptix AI simulated lifts at 92% accuracy, GS1 reduced fraud 40%. Digital now 25% of $450M budget for 2.7x ROAS. Q4 eyes 4.0x+ with chatbots. This discipline helped gross margins expand 220 bps despite inflation.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
